articles.title: 'What a F--king Mess,' NBA Exec Sounds Off on Dejounte Murray's Trade Request amid Latest Rumors
articles.summary: A "high-ranking" NBA executive from a rival team issued a blunt assessment to Kelly Iko of Yahoo Sports about the current situation in New Orleans, where the Pelicans are reportedly attempting to find a new home for guard Dejounte Murray after he issued a trade request.
articles.body:
A "high-ranking" NBA executive from a rival team issued a blunt assessment to Kelly Iko of Yahoo Sports about the current situation in New Orleans, where the Pelicans are reportedly attempting to find a new home for guard Dejounte Murray after he issued a trade request.

"What a f--king mess," the executive told Iko. "No one wants to touch him."

"As it pertains to Murray, according to sources, the thinking is simple," Iko wrote. "His unhappiness and hope for a new environment is not new and has been discussed privately since last season, with a growing sense that his reluctance to return earlier from his January 2025 Achilles tear was in hopes of being moved at last year's deadline.

"But it was rather difficult to define a market for an injured player (Murray returned later that month). The decision to draft Jeremiah Fears last summer was another clear indicator that New Orleans was open to moving in another direction, which upset Murray — echoing similar sentiments to his departures from San Antonio and Atlanta."

Murray's future NBA whereabouts are in limbo following the trade request . However, it appears finding a trade partner might be difficult as well per numerous reports.

ESPN's Brian Windhorst reported on his Hoop Collective podcast that the Pelicans sent Murray home following his trade request. In addition, his value has reportedly taken a dip (6:50 mark).

"And there's some audio that got out from some courtside microphones from a couple of days ago; I can't confirm what Dejounte, who he was talking about. People have jumped to conclusions, and I'm not saying it's wrong, but it seemed like it's a possibility that Dejounte was becoming hard to have around the team.

"So, in my discussions with teams over the last couple of days, multiple teams have told me that they view, as [Tim MacMahon] just described, I mean, this is your opinion, but it is an informed opinion, because multiple teams have told me that they view Dejounte as a distressed asset to the point where if you were to trade for him that you would want compensation in addition to him to take him."

Chris Mannix of Sports Illustrated also reported that interest in Murray might be "lukewarm at best."

"Now comes the hard part. In talking to several rival team officials, the sense is the market for Murray will be lukewarm at best. Murray's reportedly interested in a trade to Phoenix—the Suns have a need for a starting point guard and a player (Jalen Green) they can swap—but it's unclear how interested Phoenix is.

"Murray is two years removed from an Achilles tear. He played 14 games last season and is not a three-point threat. He will collect $33 million this season and has a player option for $31 million for the next one. Two team officials I talked to said they would ask for a first-round pick to absorb Murray's contract."

Murray started well over his first five games this season, averaging 18.2 points on 47.8 percent shooting, 6.2 rebounds, 5.6 assists and 2.4 blocks per game over his first five contests. That is representative of what he can bring to a team at his best. He is a talented two-way guard who provided energy and effort on the defensive end.

On the flip side, Murray can sometimes struggle with his shot. Of note, he posted 7.5 points on 33.3 percent shooting, 3.0 assists and 2.5 rebounds over his last four games. He also hasn't shot well from behind the three-point line of late (30.0 percent in 54 games since 2024-25).

The torn Achilles unfortunately kept Murray out for nearly 13 months, although he thankfully appears past that now after returning in Feb. 2026.

Ultimately, Murray's contract, which would pay him $31 million in 2027-28 should he exercise his player option, seems to be an issue here. The Pelicans made clear that they will "evaluate potential trade opportunities that are in the best interest of our organization." At the very least, they have time to do so with the deadline not until Feb. 12, 2027.

articles.title: Judge Clears the Way for Arizona's RJ Godfrey to Possibly Play in Showdown with No. 3 UConn
articles.summary: TUCSON, Ariz. (AP) — Arizona forward RJ Godfrey has been declared eligible by a Pima County judge, clearing the way for him to potentially play in the 12th-ranked Wildcats' showdown with No. 3 UConn on Wednesday.
articles.body:
TUCSON, Ariz. (AP) — Arizona forward RJ Godfrey has been declared eligible by a Pima County judge, clearing the way for him to potentially play in the 12th-ranked Wildcats' showdown with No. 3 UConn on Wednesday.

Pima County Superior Court Judge Jeffrey Bergin granted a temporary restraining order and a preliminary injunction on Tuesday that would make Godfrey eligible for the first time this season.

A Clemson transfer, Godfrey joined the Wildcats after a judge in Georgia granted an injunction clearing him and several other athletes to play this season in the wake of the NCAA's new eligibility rules. The Georgia Court of Appeals granted the NCAA a stay, leaving his future in limbo.

Godfrey and his attorneys sued the Arizona Board of Regents on Nov. 5, seeking a permanent injunction for eligibility.

Godfrey was expected to be a key piece for Arizona coming off its first Final Four appearance in 25 years after Tobe Awaka graduated.

Duke basketball has landed a commitment from one of the top international prospects out of the class of 2027.

Per Rivals' Joe Tipton, Serbian wing Matija Lukić has committed to the Blue Devils, picking Jon Scheyer's program over North Carolina, UConn and more.

Lukić is rated a 3-star prospect by 247Sports' composite rankings and is considered to be the No. 2 international player in the class of 2027.

Adam Finkelstein, 247Sports' director of scouting, described the 6'9" Lukić as a "jumbo wing with an overlap of perimeter size and well-rounded ball-skills."

Lukić joins a class that is ranked No. 3 overall for 2027, according to 247Sports . The Blue Devils have already landed commitments from 5-star small forward Asa Montgomery , the No. 8 in the 2027 recruiting class, as well as Kager Knueppel , the younger brother of Kon who is ranked No. 16 nationally.

With the addition of Lukić, Duke now has the top two international players, as they have already earned a commitment from Australian point guard Luke Paul .

The Blue Devils have a bright future ahead of them, though they're looking to win in 2026 as well. Duke is off to a 3-1 start, having dropped last week's matchup against No. 2 Michigan State. It will get another tough game on Tuesday against No. 10 Illinois before facing No. 3 UConn and top-ranked Florida at the Players Era 8 tournament.

Scheyer has found plenty of success in his first few seasons as Duke's head coach, with a pair of Elite Eight runs and a Final Four run in 2025. Still, he's chasing the national championship he was hired to deliver.

articles.title: NBA stars are missing nearly 30 games per season, and the league has done nothing about it
articles.summary: NBA stars now miss 27.7 games per season, up from 10.6 in the 1990s, as load management and back-to-backs test fan patience and league revenue.
articles.body: NBA stars are sitting out more than a quarter of games on the second night of back-to-backs this season. Even with rest between games, their participation rate is only 80%. It wasn't always this way. According to Yahoo Sports' Tom Haberstroh, NBA stars missed an average of 10.6 games per season in the 1990s. Last season, that number reached 27.7, more than two and a half times as many. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE His research shows how sharply the average number of games missed per star has risen over the decades: The article defines a "star" as a player with at least one All-Star or All-NBA selection in the previous three seasons. Given the absences already this season involving Anthony Edwards, LeBron James, Steph Curry, Luka Doncic, Kyrie Irving and Chet Holmgren, that average could surpass 30 in 2027. Though the NBA's television ratings are strong this season, stars missing this many games should concern the league. Continuing down this path risks discouraging fans from buying tickets, especially well in advance. Imagine buying NBA tickets as a Christmas gift, only to find out the biggest stars are sitting out because of injuries or load management. Further, such trends are unlikely to change without a significant change in the NBA schedule. So what is the league going to do about it? One possibility is Haberstroh's proposal: shorten the season from 82 to 65 games and eliminate back-to-backs. A shorter schedule would also give regular-season games more importance, with each win and loss carrying greater weight in the standings. The NFL should take note as talk of an 18-game season intensifies. The more games a league adds, the less each one matters. The problem with a shorter season is, of course, money. Fewer games could mean less revenue, particularly from television networks. Part of the NBA's value to its broadcast partners is the sheer volume of programming it provides. Cutting 17 games from each team's schedule could reduce what those networks are willing to pay. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Another option is shortening the games themselves. According to Sports Illustrated, NBA Commissioner Adam Silver likes the idea of cutting games from 48 to 40 minutes. Ten-minute quarters are worth considering. Shorter games could create more urgency and reduce wear and tear on players. The question is how much eliminating eight minutes would actually reduce injuries. The benefit could be marginal, particularly if back-to-backs remain. The league could also spread its schedule over a longer period. But there are issues with this scenario as well. The season already begins earlier than it once did, and extending it further risks diluting interest. The NBA has resisted playing beyond mid-June to avoid pushing deeper into summer, traditionally one of television's least-watched periods. Starting earlier would mean competing with even more football. Neither option is particularly appealing. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Ultimately, something needs to change. The NBA cannot continue a structure in which its biggest names miss nearly 30 games a season – and counting. As Haberstroh put it, "The NBA has always sold its stars. Right now, the league is breaking that promise." Between ticket prices and the streaming subscriptions required to follow the league, watching the NBA has never been more expensive. Fans shouldn't be paying more for a smaller chance of seeing the players they paid to watch And yet, that is exactly the current reality.

articles.title: Hawks' CJ McCollum out at least 4 weeks with calf strain, putting rookie Kingston Flemings in the spotlight

Atlanta Hawks guard CJ McCollum has a left calf strain and will be sidelined for at least four weeks. The Hawks announced the injury update on Tuesday.

McCollum sustained the injury in Sunday's win over the Milwaukee Bucks. Imaging has since revealed the calf strain. He'll be reevaluated in four weeks, per the Hawks.

Through 14 games, McCollum is averaging 14.5 points, 3.9 assists, 3.1 rebounds and 1.1 steals per game while shooting 43.3% from the floor and 35.2% from 3. The Hawks enter Tuesday at 8-6, tied with the Miami Heat for the fourth-best record in the Eastern Conference.

The injury is a blow for the Hawks as they lose a key playmaker and their veteran voice on the court.

McCollum, 35, began the season as Atlanta's starting point guard. But he gave way to rookie Kingston Flemings in the starting unit, recently telling the NBA on Prime that he approached head coach Quin Snyder about making the lineup change.

"I didn't like the way we were playing as a unit, as a starting unit," McCollum said. "I think we were a little sluggish. I think we were lackluster from a ball movement standpoint. "I think we were stagnant, and we have a lot of guys that can create and make plays. And I think for Kingston, he's a guy who gets downhill. He's got tremendous speed. He's learning and growing. And I think it gives him a chance to kind of develop, for us as a franchise and for us as an organization. … "The way I play, I can get to it off the bench, I can get to it as a starter. I'm mature enough to be able to handle different roles, different minutes."

"The way I play, I can get to it off the bench, I can get to it as a starter. I'm mature enough to be able to handle different roles, different minutes."

With McCollum sidelined, the keys to the offense will belong to Flemings, whom the Hawks selected with the No. 8 pick in June's draft out of Houston. In 12 games including five starts, Flemings is averaging 7.8 points, 4.1 assists, 2.5 rebounds and 0.7 steals in 21.5 minutes per game.

Flemings' shooting efficiency has stood out, especially for a rookie. He's shooting 51.4% from the field and 42.9% on 1.8 3-point attempts per game. He's done so in limited playing time as McCollum has continued to play heavy minutes off the bench.

Flemings has been day-to-day with back tightness, but was reportedly able to practice on Tuesday. He projects to have an opportunity to build on his success with increased volume and playing time in McCollum's absence.

The Hawks also announced Tuesday that second-year backup forward Asa Newell will miss at least four months with a plantar plate tear in his left great to that required surgery. Newell was averaging 3.6 points and 2.6 rebounds in 11 minutes per game in five appearances this season.

articles.title: North Carolina guard Neo Avdalas out 2 months with broken wrist suffered in loss to Georgia
articles.summary: Neo Avdalas, who transferred into North Carolina from Virginia Tech, underwent surgery on his left wrist and will now be sidelined until mid-January.
articles.body:
North Carolina will be without guard Neo Avdalas for the next two months.

Avdalas suffered a broken left wrist in their loss to Georgia last week, the school announced on Tuesday. He underwent surgery on his wrist, and is now expected to miss about eight weeks recovering.

Based on that timeline, Avdalas should be able to rejoin the Tar Heels in early to mid-January right as ACC play is getting going.

Avdalas went down in North Carolina's 78-70 loss to Georgia at the Dean Smith Center on Friday. He drove to the rim and sank a tough layup in the final minutes of the contest, but fell awkwardly to the floor and landed right on his left wrist. He remained in the game, but was clearly uncomfortable the rest of the way.

Avdalas finished the game with 14 points and three assists. The sophomore, who transferred into North Carolina from Virginia Tech earlier this year, has averaged nine points, 3.8 assists and 3.5 rebounds through the first four games of the season.

The loss on Friday was the first of the season for North Carolina, which dropped it to 3-1. It was also the first loss of the Michael Malone era. The longtime Denver Nuggets head coach took over after the Tar Heels split with Hubert Davis at the end of last season.

While Avdalas' absence will undoubtedly make things difficult, North Carolina does not have a difficult nonconference slate ahead. The Tar Heels will take on No. 20 Arkansas on Dec. 1 in its only ranked matchup before ACC play, though Kentucky, Butler, Georgetown and West Virginia all should be solid opponents.

articles.title: ‘Definitely Took That Personally,’ ‘Absurd’ – NBA Fans React As Joel Embiid Scores 37 Points for 76ers Hours After Being Labeled a ‘Liability’
articles.summary: Joel Embiid scored a season-high 37 points Monday night as the Philadelphia 76ers played without LeBron James and beat the Brooklyn Nets 135-123. The outing...
articles.body:
Joel Embiid scored a season-high 37 points Monday night as the Philadelphia 76ers played without LeBron James and beat the Brooklyn Nets 135-123. The outing comes immediately after an anonymous NBA assistant coach criticized the 2023 MVP, labeling him a "liability" in an ESPN story.

It was the first time Embiid topped 30 points this season. He shot 13-for-22 from field after entering the night at a career-worst 37.4% from the field.

Fans React as Joel Embiid Scores 37 Points for 76ers After Criticism

Entering the game, Embiid had shot 4-for-36 from 3-point range, which ranked last among players with at least 20 attempts, and 1-for-25 over his previous nine games. He had also sat out Sunday's game against the Indiana Pacers with right foot plantar fascia management, the third game he had missed this season.

That was where things stood on Monday when Dave McMenamin, who covers the NBA for ESPN, shared his latest piece .

"The most common opinion shared by folks around the league is just how important Embiid, the 2023 league MVP, will be. 'Embiid looks … like a liability,' one of the Western Conference assistant coaches said," he wrote.

While take unnamed coach took a shot at Embiid, one Western Conference scout told ESPN something very different. "The rest of the NBA better hope that Embiid never gets completely healthy. Because if he does, everyone will fight for second place."

Embiid wasted no time in Brooklyn. He scored 13 points in the first quarter and 24 in the first half, his most in any half since January of last season, as the 76ers built a 78-59 halftime lead. The 37 points were also his most in a road game since Dec. 30, 2024. He also totaled 5 rebounds, 2 blocks, and a steal.

One fan was already joking before the game ended that it "took Embiid a whole 10 hours to beat the 'liability' allegations."

Another fan tied the performance directly to the comment. "Embiid dropped 37 points after an anonymous coach called him a liability on the court. He definitely took that personally," they wrote .

A third fan was left with a question : "Do we think Joel Embiid saw that 'liability' quote?"

After the game, Embiid pointed to his own approach.

"Everything I do has to be with force, that's how I've always been successful," he said.

The label itself drew pushback, too. One fan wrote the next morning: "37 points last night in 32 minutes. Embiid is obviously past his peak, but 'liability' is absurd. He's still a very efficient scorer when needed."

Another fan pointed to how quickly the conversation had turned: "They were calling Embiid a liability just the other day."

The win moved the 76ers to 12-3, first in the Eastern Conference, and they are 4-0 this season without James.

Embiid is now averaging 19.5 points, 8.5 rebounds, 3.5 assists, 0.8 blocks, and 0.8 steals while shooting 40% from the field and 15% from 3-point range.

articles.title: El genio Hifi termina con la racha del Barça
articles.standfirst: Un triplazo del escolta del Paris Basketball a falta de 14 segundos tumba a un Barça lastrado por 22 pérdidas que llevaba nueve victorias seguidas
articles.summary: Un triplazo del escolta del Paris Basketball a falta de 14 segundos tumba a un Barça lastrado por 22 pérdidas que llevaba nueve victorias seguidas
articles.body: Nadir Hifi es uno de los jugadores más excitantes de Europa. También puede ser uno de los más desquiciantes. Porque su toma de decisiones resulta más que dudosa, pero si las mete... Así son los genios. El escolta del Paris Basketball, máximo anotador de la Euroliga, hizo 25 puntos y hundió al Barça con un triple forzadísimo sobre la defensa de Brizuela cuando restaban 14 segundos (86-89). El propio escolta azulgrana no pudo replicar en la última posesión. En el séptimo final apretado de los culés en sus últimos ocho encuentros de Euroliga no apareció Robinson, su talismán en esos momentos. Sí Hifi, que la semana pasada ya había sentenciado al Fenerbahce en la prórroga tras una actuación horrible. Se acaba la racha del Barça de nueve victorias consecutivas, cinco de ellas en la competición europea, y pierde el paso con los de arriba. Con una rotación corta por las bajas de Gibson, Núñez, Punter y Makoundou, le lastraron mucho las pérdidas. Nada menos que 22, convertidas por los parisinos en 34 puntos. También los rebotes de ataque concedidos en la segunda mitad. En esta competición no se puede regalar nada. El Paris Basketball, el equipo que más triples lanza de la Euroliga, fue fiel a su reputación. Tiró 43 y metió 14. Sus tres primeras canastas fueron desde el arco con tres tiradores distintos. El Barça aceptó el reto de inicio. Entre los dos equipos, cinco triples en tres minutos. Mandaban los visitantes pese a que Umude domaba a Hifi. A los azulgranas les señalaban dos técnicas por flopping y no cuidaban nada bien el balón ante la agresividad del rival. Al final del primer cuarto, 20-24 tras seis pérdidas locales con un Robinson desacertado. El segundo periodo fue una montaña rusa. Arriba el Barça con un 5-0. Luego el París, con un 0-12 liderado por Dokossi (25-36). Casi cuatro minutos estuvieron los culés sin anotar, pero extraviando balones como si no costara. Reacción con la intensidad de Umude y uno de esos trances anotadores que sufre Robinson. Esta vez fue antes del clutch time. Siete puntos en tres minutos para ayudar en un fulgurante parcial de 17-0. Y, por supuesto, de nuevo arriba: 42-36. Cuando todo se estabilizó llegó el descanso con 46-43. El Barça sumaba 14 pérdidas y el París había anotado 22 puntos tras ellas. De poco servía el dominio del rebote (28, con 11 ofensivos, a 17) con un Nebo colosal, ya con nueve. Las subidas y bajadas no se quedaron en el vestuario. Robinson, que hizo sólo tres puntos en la segunda parte, y Umude abrían un hueco ilusionante (55-43), pero el París reaccionó como sabe, con triples. Balcerowski, sensacional tras el intermedio, se imponía en la pintura hasta conseguir sus topes en la Euroliga: 17 puntos y 29 de valoración. Le faltó concretar los +1. Un tapón de Minaya a Hifi y posterior triple volvió a despegar a los locales. Tampoco el 66-56 fue la escapada definitiva. El Barça se secó ante la subida física gala y Morgan, sobre la bocina, mandó el partido en un pañuelo al último acto: 69-68. Ahí se creció Hifi anotando y asistiendo (8). Los azulgranas se perdían entre disruptivas y revisiones de los árbitros mientras se iban quedando atrás (74-79). Llegaba el momento de Robinson, pero no apareció. Fueron Balcerowski y el empuje de Parra, que se llevó dos golpes en la cabeza, los que tiraron. Minaya igualó a 84 con un triple, pero había aparecido Johnson, que hizo sus dos únicas canastas en el tramo final. Nebo volvió a empatar, a 86, tras su enésimo rebote ofensivo y un mate en el que recibió una falta no pitada. Restaban 34 segundos. Balón para Hifi. Excitante. Con un toque desquiciante. Letal. 86 - Barcelona (20+26+23+17): Robinson (15), Martin (7), Umude (8), Parra (11), Nebo (7) -cinco inicial-, Brizuela (8), Ubal (2), Balcerowski (17), Nkamhoua (5) y Minaya (6). 89 - París Basketball (24+19+25+21): Hifi (25), Tarpei (3), Herrera (11), Warren (8), Faye (8) -cinco inicial-, Rodhen (5), Etienne (10), Dokossi (11), Johnson (4), Morgan (3), Ntilikina (1) y Pereira (0). articles.title: OKC native Blake Griffin says taxpayers 'hamstrung' on $900M Thunder arena deal
articles.summary: Blake Griffin questions the $850 million public cost of the new Thunder arena, citing Oklahoma teacher pay needs.
articles.body:
Oklahoma native Blake Griffin recently took aim at the taxpayer cost of the Oklahoma City Thunder 's new arena, asking whether those dollars could be better spent on teacher pay and other public needs.

On the latest episode of his Prime show, "The Stepback with Blake Griffin," the former NBA player used the illustration of Oklahoma City to kick off a deep dive into how groups pay for sports stadiums and who might be negatively affected.

In December 2023, 71% of Oklahoma City voters approved a six-year, 1% sales tax that will provide at least $850 million in public funding for a new Thunder arena, while the team's ownership group will contribute $50 million. As part of the deal, the Thunder agreed to remain in Oklahoma City through at least 2050.

Griffin highlighted a quote from professor J.C. Bradbury of Kennesaw State University, who told the Associated Press at the time of the vote: "It is by far the worst stadium deal I've ever seen negotiated from a public standpoint."

"But what choice do fans really have?" Griffin asked. Fans might have to watch Shai Gilgeous-Alexander play for the "Wichita Thunder," Griffin joked.

The Oklahoma City native and former University of Oklahoma player knows how much the Thunder means to the community he grew up in, adding that "it was super exciting" when the Seattle SuperSonics uprooted their dynasty to the Oklahoma City metro in 2008.

But the SuperSonics left the Pacific Northwest after 41 years in the area when a $500 million plan to build an arena outside Seattle failed in Washington's state legislature.

Griffin suggested that instead, tax dollars slated to keep the Thunder in town could have been used on other projects.

He mentioned the state's low national ranking in teacher pay, where Oklahoma ranks 47th according to the National Education Association .

"Which matters to me because both my parents were teachers and now they're paying for that stadium," Griffin said. "Well, not just the two of them. A lot of people."

"But fans feel hamstrung having to pay billions of dollars to keep the teams they love," Griffin said.

Where does Oklahoma City Thunder's new arena stand today?

Developments on the new Continental Coliseum, set to open in 2028 , are still underway since breaking ground in March 2026.

Continental Coliseum is being built on the site of the former arena and convention center on the block bounded by Reno Avenue, Ron Norick Boulevard, Sheridan Avenue and E.K. Gaylord Boulevard. It is planned to be open in time for the 2028-2029 season.

The new arena, like Paycom Center, will host a variety of events beyond basketball. From top touring artists to family shows to national sporting events, the venue is expected to become a top destination in the region for live experiences.

New renderings show interior of Oklahoma City's new NBA arena

New renderings , released in October 2026, showcase what some of the food and beverage spaces inside Continental Coliseum could look like.

Among the new designs, developers are planning out bar spaces with enclosed seating lounges, bar-top dining and other social spaces, which will allow fans to gather before, during and after events. Levy is also planning to introduce dedicated speed lanes during non-NBA events, which are aimed at helping guests move seamlessly through service points and return to the action faster than before.

Developers say the coliseum will offer a significant and "very intentional increase" in its culinary infrastructure, including 17 kitchens and a 33% higher point-of-sale per person ratio.

The completion of the arena will also renew the Oklahoma City Thunder's 25-year commitment to remain in Oklahoma City. The $900 million arena will cover at least 750,000 square feet in the heart of Downtown OKC.

articles.title: Jimmy Butler, Draymond Green Floated as Warriors Trade Deadline Candidates by NBA Insider
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors may decide to part ways with Jimmy Butler and Draymond Green on the trade market before the 2026-27 deadline.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors may decide to part ways with Jimmy Butler and Draymond Green on the trade market before the 2026-27 deadline.

ESPN's Marc J. Spears brought up Butler and Green as potential trade candidates during a Tuesday appearance on NBA Today .

"I think they need to be aggressive at the trade deadline," Spears said regarding the Warriors (5:25 mark). "They have some pieces to do it. There might be some people that have been there for awhile that could be traded."

"Draymond, Jimmy. I do expect the Warriors to make some kind of splash at the trade deadline," he added.

The Warriors could decide to part ways with Butler, who's 37 years old and is currently recovering from a torn ACL . He'll earn $56.8 million for the 2026-27 season before hitting free agency next summer (via Spotrac ).

As for Green, he's also set to become a free agent in 2027 after receiving $27.7 million during his 2026-27 campaign. The four-time All-Star is 36 years old.

Nick Friedell of The Athletic previously reported that Butler and Green "have expressed interest in retiring with the Warriors, though doing so could require them to return on substantially smaller contracts."

Still, Golden State might explore a change of scenery for them on the trade market as the organization looks to build around Stephen Curry and standout rookie Yaxel Lendeborg.

The Warriors have opened the 2026-27 season with an 8-6 record, although they're currently in the midst of a three-game losing streak.

articles.title: Kawhi Leonard Injury Update, Raptors Give Latest Return Timeline Amid Star's Rehab on Knee
articles.summary: The Toronto Raptors announced that star forward Kawhi Leonard has "progressed in his strength and conditioning program" on Tuesday after he received treatment to "address left knee swelling," per ESPN's Marc J. Spears.
articles.body:
The Toronto Raptors announced that star forward Kawhi Leonard has "progressed in his strength and conditioning program" on Tuesday after he received treatment to "address left knee swelling," per ESPN's Marc J. Spears .

Another update regarding Leonard's recovery will be provided by the team in one week, per Spears.

The seven-time All-Star has been sidelined since Oct. 23 due to left knee issues.

On Oct. 27, ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Leonard would miss "a period of weeks" due to the swelling in his left knee.

Two days later, NBA insider Chris Haynes reported that the 35-year-old was expected to be out for at least three-to-four weeks until he'd be able to return.

Leonard is beginning his second stint on the Raptors after they acquired him in a blockbuster trade with the Los Angeles Clippers during the offseason. He signed a two-year, $115 million contract with Toronto following the swap.

Leonard initially played for the Raptors during the 2018-19 season, helping them finish with a 58-24 record before winning the NBA Finals. He earned Finals MVP honors in the process.

He eventually joined the Clippers as a free agent in 2019, remaining with the organization until he came back to Toronto this year.

Leonard is coming off a 2025-26 campaign in which he averaged 27.9 points, 6.4 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.9 steals per game while shooting 50.5 percent from the field and 38.7 percent from three-point territory.

Across two games with Toronto this season, he's scored 39 points on 12-of-37 shooting in 52 minutes on the floor.

The Raptors currently own a 5-8 record, sitting at No. 9 in the Eastern Conference standings.

articles.title: LeBron James Sues Makers of AI Sports-Betting App, Saying They Used His Likeness and Nickname
articles.summary: NBA superstar LeBron James sued the makers of an AI sports-betting app Tuesday, saying they have deliberately violated his publicity rights and trademarks by calling it "Bron" and using artificially generated images of him in their marketing.
articles.body:
NBA superstar LeBron James sued the makers of an AI sports-betting app Tuesday, saying they have deliberately violated his publicity rights and trademarks by calling it "Bron" and using artificially generated images of him in their marketing.

In a lawsuit filed in U.S. District Court in New York, James' attorneys called it "a willful, bad-faith tactic" to use the player's fame, likeness and nickname to promote "a new and unknown product."

The complaint asks the court to block the makers from using the Philadelphia 76ers star's name, to give up any money they've already made, and to award damages — including fair market value for the use of his name as well as punitive damages.

LBJ Picked Up 'Bad Habits' Trying to Imitate MJ

"Defendants did not care that they had engaged in illegal conduct to gain notoriety for their previously unknown app," the lawsuit states. "They intentionally created the false impression that Mr. James endorsed and was affiliated with their Bron App, in an effort to drive downloads and paid subscriptions."

Messages sent by The Associated Press through the app's website and to email addresses for its founders seeking comment were not immediately returned Tuesday.

The app's developer, PlayVision Inc., is based in California. It was launched by Chief Executive Anish Gupta and Chief Technology Officer Marc Zoghby in 2025, with backing from the startup accelerator Y Combinator, as a program that would use artificial intelligence to analyze game and practice footage for sports teams and fans.

This year, the company released its "Bron" app, which it says does not take direct wagers but charges a subscription fee for services like bet tracking and odds comparisons. It launched a marketing campaign this month that featured an image of a person resembling James — down to his tattoos, voice and number 23 jersey — sitting in a locker room and scrolling through the app.

James' lawyers sent a cease-and-desist letter, as previously reported by Front Office Sports . The company took the ad down, but not before it had been reposted and viewed about 1 million times, the lawsuit said.

Gupta responded to the attorneys' demand on social media by writing that the app would get a new name, but no new name had been adopted by the time the lawsuit was filed, leading James' legal team to suggest the company was milking the controversy for attention. Gupta wrote on social media this week that the new name will be announced Wednesday.

The lawsuit notes that James typically commands tens of millions of dollars for such endorsement deals, and that he already has an exclusive deal with the prediction market platform Polymarket. It alleges that the app's marketing was especially harmful in part because it showed the AI-generated James scrolling through bets involving NBA players.

"The integrity of NBA competition — and the public's confidence that players are not betting on the games they play — is of paramount importance to the league, its players, and its fans," the lawsuit said. "Any suggestion that an active NBA player is betting on NBA games is therefore far from a trivial matter, and it should not be used for clicks and views."

articles.title: No. 25 LSU Adds RJ Luis Jr., Who Briefly Was Under Contract With 2 NBA Teams, To Its Roster
articles.summary: LSU added RJ Luis Jr., who briefly spent time under contract with two NBA teams, to its roster on Tuesday, a day before the 25th-ranked Tigers' scheduled game against Louisiana-Monroe.
articles.body:
LSU added RJ Luis Jr., who briefly spent time under contract with two NBA teams, to its roster on Tuesday, a day before the 25th-ranked Tigers' scheduled game against Louisiana-Monroe.

The move comes after LSU President Wade Rousse released a statement saying the university intended to comply with a district court ruling in Baton Rouge that said the NCAA and Southeastern Conference could not declare Luis ineligible or punish LSU for allowing Luis to play.

"LSU is committed to compliance with NCAA and SEC rules, but it is equally committed to obeying the orders of Louisiana's courts," Rousse said.

The SEC called LSU's decision "deeply concerning and disappointing."

"LSU's decision today to rely on its own interpretation of the court's order to justify its actions is inconsistent with the expectations and responsibilities of membership in the Southeastern Conference," the league said in a statement. "The conference will continue to uphold and defend the standards and policies established by its member universities."

Luis, the 2025 Big East player of the Year with St. John's, spent parts of the 2025 NBA offseason with the Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics. He now joins a team that has won its first four games and this week entered the AP Top 25 on the heels of victory on Saturday over then-No. 14 Gonzaga.

"LSU, by rostering RJ, did the right thing," Luis' lawyer, Tony Clayton, told The Associated Press, noting that Luis never played in a regular-season NBA game and that the NCAA routinely issues waivers allowing players from professional leagues overseas to play for college teams in the United States.

LSU has three such international players on its roster: centers Brice Dessert and Michael Ruzic and forward Saliou Niang.

"It would be fundamentally unfair to RJ Luis to not allow him to play college ball when you have so many similarly situated young men who are playing in college now," Clayton said.

State district judge Ronald R. Johnson in East Baton Rouge Parish issued an injunction against the NCAA in Luis' case on Aug. 24 . But the SEC shortly afterward strengthened rules against athletes who'd signed NFL, NBA or WNBA contracts , adding enforcement provisions that included fines of up to 50% of a program's revenue and half-season suspensions for coaches.

Johnson subsequently ruled that the SEC could not punish LSU for allowing Luis to play, and that LSU could not cite SEC rules as a reason for keeping Luis off its roster.

In his statement, Rousse noted that Luis "secured his eligibility through a court order before the new SEC policy interpretation was announced. LSU supports the updated policy going forward, and we remain a proud and committed member of the SEC."

Rousse also noted that the SEC had confirmed to LSU that it would abide by the state court rulings in Luis' case.

LSU coach Will Wade, now in his second stint with the university that fired him in 2022 over NCAA recruiting violations, initially held off on placing Luis on the roster while the district court ruling was challenged in state appeals courts.

Last Friday, the Louisiana Supreme Court upheld Johnson's preliminary injunction against the NCAA, the SEC and LSU.

Whether Luis will remain on the roster for the entire season is unclear. That depends on how aggressively the NCAA and SEC continue to pursue the case, and the court's timeline.

Clayton, who declared after a previous favorable ruling in an eligibility case that justice was served to SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey "like a cold cup of gumbo," said he hopes the Luis matter can be settled amicably.

"I would love to sit down with Sankey and buy him a hot cup of gumbo," Clayton said. "We've got to move forward. We've got to put it behind us. I just hope they allow this kid to live his life."

articles.title: Stephen Curry's biggest smile may have come from watching son Cannon deliver a flawless 10-point performance
articles.summary: Stephen Curry has spent much of his NBA career making difficult shots look routine.
articles.body: Stephen Curry has spent much of his NBA career making difficult shots look routine. But his latest memorable basketball moment had little to do with the Warriors or another milestone in his own career. The 38-year-old guard watched his eight-year-old son, Canon Curry, put together a perfect shooting performance during an elementary school game. Canon finished with 10 points, converting all five of his attempts. For Stephen, watching from the crowd offered a different kind of satisfaction. His son was enjoying the game on his own terms, even as the Curry family name brought extra attention to the performance.How did Canon Curry put together his perfect shooting performance?Canon's 10-point outing stood out because he did not miss a single attempt. Going 5-for-5 is an impressive return for any player, but it carries an added connection when the player watching from the sidelines is one of basketball's greatest shooters.Stephen has often shared small stories about his son's personality around the game. During a 2022 appearance on Dubs Talk, the Warriors star recalled how Canon was already developing his own approach to shooting rather than simply following instructions from his father.Curry explained that his young son was not always interested in copying his advice. Canon's response was direct: "No, this is how I'm doing it."Those moments offer a glimpse of a child who enjoys basketball but is also comfortable doing things his own way. His latest performance adds another chapter to that story. However, one elementary school game is not a measure of what his future in basketball will look like. For now, the perfect shooting record is enough to celebrate.Stephen Curry's family outings offer a glimpse beyond basketballStephen's presence at Canon's game fits into a pattern of making time for his children outside his demanding NBA schedule. Earlier in November, he took Canon and his older daughter Riley to Levi's Stadium to watch the San Francisco 49ers face the Las Vegas Raiders.The family watched from a suite as San Francisco secured a 38-17 victory. Stephen also spent time with Bay Area rapper E-40 during the outing.Canon has also shared moments with his father's former Warriors teammate Klay Thompson. Earlier this month, he joined Stephen in greeting Thompson before the Miami Heat's visit to Chase Center. Thompson spent 13 seasons in Golden State, winning four championships alongside Curry.These appearances show how Stephen includes his children in different parts of his life, whether it is an NFL afternoon or a reunion with a former teammate.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Andrej Stojakovic Makes History in Illinois' Win vs. Duke, Full Box Score, Top Highlights
articles.summary: Illinois guard Andrej Stojaković made history as he led his team to a 99-78 road win over Duke on Tuesday night.
articles.body:
Illinois guard Andrej Stojaković made history as he led his team to a 99-78 road win over Duke on Tuesday night.

Stojaković finished with 46 points, representing the most by any visiting player at Cameron Indoor Stadium. His performance also marked the second-highest scoring total by any individual Duke opponent in a single game.

Neither team was able to gain much separation early in the first half, as the score was tied 22-22 just over 11 minutes into the game.

Illinois went on a 12-2 run to gain its first double-digit lead of the night, though.

While Duke quickly bounced back and cut the deficit to five points, the Fighting Illini pushed their advantage back to 10 points once again and maintained a 42-32 edge at halftime.

Illinois eventually gained a 51-35 lead in the second half and never looked back, as the Blue Devils weren't able to pull to within single digits for the remainder of the contest.

The Fighting Illini led by as many as 23 points in the second half, cruising to the win.

Illinois thrived around the rim throughout the victory, grabbing 54 rebounds compared to just 34 for Duke. The Fighting Illini also scored 48 points in the paint, while the Blue Devils finished with just 30.

Duke suffered its first non-conference loss at Cameron Indoor Stadium by at least 20 points since joining the ACC for the 1953-54 season (h/t ESPN's Jeff Borzello ).

As for Stojaković, he continued his hot start to his 2026-27 campaign.

The son of three-time NBA All-Star Peja Stojaković already entered Tuesday's action averaging 22.3 points, 5.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists per game while shooting 61.8 percent from the field.

articles.title: Andrej Stojaković makes history with 46-point effort at Cameron Indoor while No. 10 Illinois throttles No. 5 Duke
articles.summary: Stojaković starred as the Fighting Illini put an end to the longest active home win streak in Division I men's college basketball.
articles.body:
Duke sophomore wing Dame Sarr tried to rile up Cameron Indoor Stadium less than three minutes into the second half on Tuesday night in a top-10 matchup that wasn't going the Blue Devils' way. Illinois senior guard Andrej Stojaković quelled that brief, inspired raucous.

After an impassioned Sarr raised his hand to encourage the "Cameron Crazies," he gave Illinois' Quentin Coleman a shove. The freshman guard sold the impact, resulting in a dead-ball technical being assessed to Sarr. Stojaković made the corresponding two free throws, resuming his takeover game in the wake of a 20-point first half. Because of the tech, Illinois kept the ball, and Stojaković went on to follow his own miss with a putback and-1.

Stojaković calmly pushed his hands toward the floor, motioning for everyone to settle down. He was in control. So were the No. 10 Fighting Illini (4-1), who thoroughly outplayed No. 5 Duke (3-2) most of the night, snapping the longest active home win streak in Division I men's college basketball.

Illinois' 99-78 road triumph ended a string of 35 straight Duke home wins.

Stojaković, the son of three-time NBA All-Star Peja Stojaković, piled up a career-high 46 points, the most a visitor has ever scored at Cameron Indoor. South Carolina's Grady Wallace previously held the record, having scored 43 points there in 1957.

Coleman, already an NBA Draft lottery prospect, shined as well, finishing with 27 points. Brad Underwood's team, which lost to then-No. 16 Texas Tech last week, made a statement this time out.

As for Duke, it's sitting with two losses. The Blue Devils dropped two regular-season games total in 2025-26.

During the first half, Stojaković carried an Illinois starting lineup that featured three freshmen in the absence of sophomore forward David Mirkovic and senior forward Jake Davis. Mirkovic is still working his way back from offseason foot surgery and a preseason appendectomy. Davis, meanwhile, is nursing a separated shoulder that required a recent procedure.

There was a point on Tuesday when Stojaković was 4 of 4 from the field and the rest of the Illini were 2 of 14. He wound up making his first five field-goal attempts and accounting for 19 of his team's first 31 points.

Initially, the Blue Devils established an early lead. Along the way, sophomore guard Cayden Boozer turned a steal into a transition opportunity, pushing the pace, spinning and delivering an over-the-shoulder pass to a trailing Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje. The 17-year-old freshman threw down a thundering dunk to ignite a Duke frenzy.

Yet the Blue Devils struggled from outside in the game's infancy and never really found a shooting groove in the opening frame. Senior guards Caleb Foster and John Blackwell combined for four 3s, except, collectively, Duke went a ghastly 5 of 20 from beyond the arc and 9 of 31 from the floor overall in the first half.

Plus, it piled up eight turnovers in the process. Jon Scheyer's squad was outworked on the glass, where Illinois feasted for offensive rebounds. The Blue Devils were also overpowered in the paint.

That's where Stojaković led the charge, fueling a 15-2 run that put the Illini up 34-24. The sequence forced Scheyer to call a timeout about six minutes prior to intermission. Coleman was key in that crucial stretch. He answered a rim-rattling alley-oop dunk from Duke junior center Patrick Ngongba II with a corner 3 and then drew a charge on the other end.

Scheyer wasn't happy about the call and got T'd up. Stojaković drilled the subsequent free throws and then dropped in a layup. From there, Underwood's team built on its momentum.

Duke registered only one field goal in the final five minutes of the first half. Illinois took a 42-32 advantage into the break. A snapshot of the Illini's dominance was fifth-year center Zvonimir Ivisic blocking a Boozer floater and promptly capping a give-and-go with a slam.

Illinois' first 22 points of the second half were scored by either Coleman or Stojaković.

Even though the Blue Devils emerged from halftime with heightened intensity, that energetic resurgence wasn't enough, especially after Sarr's technical spurred a 7-0 Illini run.

Duke teased a potential comeback in the middle of the final period. The Blue Devils shrunk a 23-point deficit to 12. Senior forward Drew Scharnowski offered a boost off the bench with seven timely points. He hit a 3-pointer, as did Boumtje Boumtje and freshman guard Bryson Howard.

That said, in a game that came with a combined 47 personal fouls, Stojaković and Coleman's free throws disrupted the kind of swing Duke needed.

Stojaković clocked out 16 of 20 from the charity stripe. Coleman was 13 of 15 from the free-throw line.

The Blue Devils were paced by Boumtje Boumtje's 17 points. Foster wasn't far behind with 15. Blackwell fouled out with seven points and about eight minutes left.

Stojaković's historic performance began with him surgically dissecting the interior of Duke's defense. He slashed and contorted inside, en route to a 14-of-21 shooting night that included two triples.

He was ultimately two points shy of Duke's Dick Groat for the most points any player has ever scored in Cameron Indoor. Groat put up 48 in 1952.

Stojaković was largely responsible for handing Duke a seismic defeat, which, according to ESPN , is the Blue Devils' first non-conference loss at Cameron by 20-plus points since joining the ACC in 1953-54.

articles.title: El peso del poliamor en el primer anillo que ganó LeBron James con los Cavaliers
articles.standfirst: La cantante y actriz Teyana Taylor ha revelado que, durante su matrimonio con Iman Shumpert, la idea de tener tríos fue suya: "Todo fue idea mía"
articles.summary: La cantante y actriz Teyana Taylor ha revelado que, durante su matrimonio con Iman Shumpert, la idea de tener tríos fue suya: "Todo fue idea mía"
articles.body: Iman Shumpert, jugador que ganó la NBA en 2016 en la histórica remontada de los Cleveland Cavaliers de LeBron James ante los Golden State Warriors del 73-9, vuelve a ser noticia 10 años después. Apenas un año antes Shumpert había firmado un contrato de cuatro años por valor de 40 millones de dólares y, posteriormente, contrajo matrimonio con su novia, Teyana Taylor. La pareja tuvo dos hijas, pero lo que parecía una vida idílica terminó en un tumultuoso divorcio en 2024. Iman Shumpert, que fue el número 17 del Draft de 2011 y colgó las botas en 2021, ganó más de 48 millones de dólares en sus 10 años de carrera en la NBA repartidos entre Knicks, Cavaliers, Kings, Rockets y Nets. La actriz y cantante Teyana Taylor, que vive el mejor momento de su carrera profesional tras ganar un Globo de Oro y ser nominada a los Premios Óscar por su aclamado papel en la película 'Una batalla tras otra', ha decidido tirar de la manta y hace públicos detalles de su intimidad con Iman Shumpert. "No soy una persona polígama, pero todo el mundo se enteró de que mi marido y yo habíamos tenido tríos. Decían algo así como: 'Ah, ella es capaz de hacer eso con tal de retener a un hombre'. Pero, en realidad, fue idea mía", confesó la famosa actriz. Teyana Taylor subrayó que "fue cosa mía. Me molesta que la gente piense que siempre tiene que haber un hombre que desee este tipo de cosas. En este caso, fui yo quien introdujo la dinámica poliamorosa en la relación; le planteé la idea a mi marido y simplemente le dije: 'Oye, esto es lo que quiero hacer. A la gente le sorprende que las mujeres sean las que inicien ciertas cosas". "Una mujer también puede hacer estas cosas porque ella misma lo desea", sentenció. Por su parte Iman Shumpert, dolido tras su ruptura con Teyana Taylor, reconoció que "no sé si volveré a casarme, al menos legalmente. No quiero firmar papeles ni nada por el estilo. O sea, podemos hacer un contrato; un contrato sobre algo en lo que ambos estamos trabajando de todos modos... No, paso de todo eso".

articles.title: LaMelo Ball's steal sets up Wolves' go-ahead layup, then Trey Lyles makes game-saving block vs. Trail Blazers
articles.summary: A pair of defensive plays made the difference for Minnesota on a night when its own Ayo Dosunmu erupted for a season-high 30 points.
articles.body:
While starring for the Charlotte Hornets, LaMelo Ball was far too often a defensive liability. The 25-year-old guard isn't even a month into his first regular season with the Minnesota Timberwolves, and they're already squeezing significantly more effort out of him on that end of the court.

That uptick in defensive intensity helped deliver the Wolves a 106-105 victory on Tuesday night at home against the Portland Trail Blazers.

With 8.1 seconds remaining, and Minnesota trailing by one point, Ball got a piece of an inbounds pass from Portland's Donovan Clingan, poking it free. Wolves guard Ayo Dosunmu corralled the loose ball and flipped on the accelerator. Rather than attacking the paint on a night he scored a season-high 30 points, the guard fired a pass down low to forward Jaden McDaniels, who quickly dropped in the go-ahead layup with 2.6 ticks to go.

With his team suddenly down one, Clingan connected on his next inbounds pass, as the big man hit star guard Damian Lillard in stride. Except Lillard's drive was denied by an elevating Trey Lyles. The 6-foot-9 veteran rejected the shot out of bounds.

Portland got one last chance with a second remaining on the clock. Robert Williams III couldn't handle the lob from Clingan; however, the ball ended up with Toumani Camara, whose last-second attempt was contested by Ball in the paint and off the mark.

Ball let out a triumphant roar as the buzzer sounded. He finished with 18 points on 7-of-17 shooting, but his defense down the stretch was pivotal. As for Lyles, he chipped in 8 points, 7 rebounds, 4 assists and that game-saving block in 31 minutes off the bench.

McDaniels' final basket gave him 22 points. He had a team-high three steals.

Altogether, the Timberwolves (11-4) held off a Trail Blazers (9-5) team that was fueled by a combined 48 points from Lillard (25) and his backcourt partner, Jrue Holiday (23).

Minnesota currently leads the NBA in defensive rating . It is in the top 10 of that category for the fifth straight season. This time around, Ball is part of that display, adopting the Wolves' defensive DNA .

articles.standfirst: La racha de 12 victorias consecutivas era la mejor de los Spurs en más de una década
articles.summary: La racha de 12 victorias consecutivas era la mejor de los Spurs en más de una década
articles.body: Los Detroit Pistons derrotaron por 93-105 a los San Antonio Spurs con 27 puntos de Cade Cunningham y 25 de Daniss Jenkins y cortaron la racha de 12 victorias que acumulaban Victor Wembanyama y los suyos. Los Spurs (12-3) parecían imparables en este inicio de temporada, con un Wembanyama excelso, sus bases complementándose y aún a la espera de Tobias Harris, su refuerzo veraniego, que se recupera de una lesión. Pero este martes se toparon con unos Pistons (9-4) correosos, que están buscando la fórmula para competir con los grandes después de su fracaso en los 'playoff' de la pasada temporada, tras haber liderado la Conferencia Este. Cunningham se apoyó en Jenkins para repartir la carga ofensiva de los Pistons, una ayuda esencial a la espera del regreso de Jalen Duren. A sus respectivos 27 y 25 puntos, Ausar Thompson rozó el triple-doble con 14 puntos, 9 rebotes, 12 asistencias y 5 robos. Los Pistons lanzaron con un 53,5 % de acierto en la primera mitad, necesario para resistir el arreón de los Spurs e incluso marcharse al descanso con un punto de ventaja (54-55). Además, mostraron una gran concentración durante todo el partido, con solo nueve pérdidas que dieron a los Spurs apenas 14 puntos. Para los Spurs, Wembanyama firmó 25 puntos y 18 rebotes y dejó dos jugadas para los resúmenes con autopase contra el tablero para el 'alley-oop'. Dylan Harper sumó 20 puntos, pero abandonó la pista en el último minuto de partido tras resbalar y sentir molestias musculares. Los Spurs pagaron sus propias pérdidas (13 para 22 puntos de los Pistons) y la poca puntería desde el perímetro (un 22,5 % tras acertar solo 9 de 40 lanzamientos). San Antonio no perdía un partido desde el 23 de octubre, hace casi un mes, cuando cayeron, también en el Frost Bank Center, ante los Houston Rockets de Kevin Durant. La racha de doce victorias consecutivas era la mejor de los Spurs en más de una década, desde las trece que encadenaron en la temporada 2015-16. Los Pistons no cortaban una racha de tal calibre desde 1969 contra los New York Knicks.

articles.title: Quentin Grimes matches Kobe Bryant mark with 10 3-pointers, drops career-high 47 points to lift Lakers past Hornets
articles.summary: Quentin Grimes hit a 3-pointer in the final moments of regulation to force overtime on Tuesday night at Crypto.com Arena.
articles.body:
It took a historic outing from Quentin Grimes, but the Los Angeles Lakers' winning streak is alive and well.

Grimes hit 10 3-pointers, including a clutch bucket at the end of regulation to force overtime at Crypto.com Arena, to lift the Lakers to a 118-114 win over the Charlotte Hornets. Grimes finished the night with a career-high 47 points in the outing and went 10-of-14 from behind the arc.

Grimes is now one of just two players in Lakers franchise history to record 10 made 3-pointers in a single game, joining Hall of Famer Kobe Bryant, who hit 12 in a game back in 2003.

For a long time on Tuesday night, it looked as if the Hornets were going to run away with the game. They built up an 18-point lead in the third quarter, and limited the Lakers to just a layup from Grimes over nearly a six-minute span in the period. The game felt over.

But the Lakers slowly chipped away at that lead to get into position to make it a game again down the stretch. That's when Grimes drilled his most important bucket. With just seconds left on the clock and the Lakers down by three, Grimes caught a perfect pass from Luka Dončić and sank his shot from the wing.

At that point, any momentum that the Hornets had was gone. The Lakers outscored them 7-3 in the extra frame to secure the four-point win.

Grimes went 16-of-24 from the field, and had six rebounds and three assists to go with his 47-point outing. Grimes joined the Lakers this past offseason on a four-year, $60 million deal in free agency after spending last season with the Philadelphia 76ers.

"At times, it felt like he was single-handedly bringing us back," Lakers coach JJ Redick said of Grimes, via the OC Register's Benjamin Royer .

Dončić had 36 points, seven assists and six rebounds in the win for the Lakers. They have now won nine consecutive games and sit at 13-3 on the season, which is the best record in the league.

Brandon Miller led the Hornets with 28 points in the loss, which dropped them to 4-10 on the season. Naz Reid added 23 points and 11 rebounds, and Coby White finished with 19 points.

While Tuesday night's game had a thrilling finish, the Lakers won't have much time to recover. They'll host the Utah Jazz next on Wednesday night in their third back-to-back of the season.

But at least for now, the Lakers' winning streak, and place atop the league standings, is safe.
